newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler sees no sign of interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler sees no sign of interest rate rise.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Sunday he saw no signs at present to suggest a rise in German interest rates.
The current development of all fundamental economic factors ran counter to an interest rate increase, Zeitler told Bayerischer Rundfunk in an interview broadcast on Sunday.
He said inflation was weak and money supply was growing at a moderate pace. But despite the low inflation rate of 1.5 percent in 1996, Zeitler added: "Inflation is never dead."

Zeitler, who is president of the state central bank of Bavaria, said he saw no reason to expect an increase in interest rates linked to the launch of European monetary union, scheduled for January 1, 1999.
"I see no reason at all why markets should depart from their expectation of medium-term stability," he said.
"Interest rate fears" or "interest rate fatalism" displayed in some quarters were unfounded, he added.
Zeitler said that Germany's share market faced a "considerable boost" from plans to introduce pension funds.
He said the market had already received a push from the flotation of Deutsche Telekom AG last November.
